comparator.name: Business Administration
comparator.sourceNotes: The Dutch-taught, part-time degree includes 110 EC of compulsory business courses, 25 EC of academic skills, 30 EC of open electives and a 15 EC thesis. The published timetable illustrates a six-year study pace.

courses: Business & Economy in the Age of AI

core: Business administration: how organisations and businesses function and management problems are solved
Accounting, finance and economics of the business environment
Research methods and academic research within organisations
Business ethics, governance and the institutional environment
adjacent: Business resilience and leading organisational and societal transitions
Accounting, finance and quantitative economic analysis
questions: Supply chains, resilience and circular operations
Analysing practice-based business cases and contemporary management problems

trace: develops accounting theory and financial-statement analysis for understanding how economic events affect business
AI adoption, market structure, business models and governance support analysis of organizational change.
covers the legal frameworks for contracts, trade, investment and dispute resolution that govern business activity
Financial markets, valuation and banking risk extend the study of business finance.
provides micro- and macroeconomic principles on firms, market structure and macroeconomic conditions as the economic environment of organisations
examines growth, inflation, business cycles, international trade and fiscal and monetary policy as the macroeconomic environment of organisations

examines market failure, taxation, public spending and government intervention that shape the economic environment of firms and financial decisions

develops product-innovation practice in a team that mimics a design-and-development firm, from customer needs to prototype
examines marketing strategy, consumer behaviour and brand strategy through case studies and marketing plans
develops strategic planning from vision to execution and digital business-model transformation using industry cases
develops applied market research, from planning and data gathering through analysis to managerial recommendations
examines the institutional, political and cultural forces on global business, including cross-border governance and corporate responsibility
develops venture creation, business models and market validation in a team start-up project, covering the entrepreneurial foundations of business administration
provides research design, survey and experimental methods and descriptive and inferential statistics for studying organisational questions
develops leadership theory, self-awareness and applied leadership practice
develops leadership communication and ethical influence using leadership models and organisational-communication cases
examines diversity management and inclusive leadership in organisations
examines motivation, group dynamics, organisational culture and structure through organisational-behaviour case work
develops negotiation theory and practice through simulations as a strategic managerial skill
develops data cleaning, visualisation and manipulation for evidence-based analysis of business and economic data
introduces regression, classification and prediction techniques for modelling and forecasting economic and business data
Python and debugging provide a computational basis for business data analysis.
provides calculus and mathematical techniques underlying quantitative economic and financial modelling
provides linear-algebra foundations for regression, econometric and data-analysis methods
provides probability, estimation and simulation foundations for statistical inference and risk in finance and economics
examines circular-economy strategies and technologies for resource security, recovery and stewardship
examines governance and collective decision-making by governmental and non-governmental actors in sustainability transitions
examines sustainable farming systems and innovation as a production-side resilience question for food supply chains
provides the planetary-boundaries and sustainability foundations needed to analyse business resilience and societal transitions
extends sustainability foundations toward technical analysis of transition technologies
examines the drivers, impacts and societal transformations of climate change to which organisations must respond
develops life-cycle analysis and circular-economy evaluation of products across their whole life cycle, supporting analysis of supply chains and circular operations
combines technical and economic analysis of renewable-energy options with a report to a partner company
provides the moral-theory foundations (virtue ethics, deontology, utilitarianism) on which ethical analysis of managerial decisions rests
Policy diagnosis and memos connect firm transitions to regulatory choices and competing interests.
develops qualitative research design and analysis for studying social processes
examines social-movement theory and environmental justice as stakeholder and societal pressures that drive transitions
provides multivariable statistics and experimental methods used in business analytics and market research
examines how the climate crisis is communicated and contested, supporting stakeholder communication in transitions

alternatives.label: Business, Management and Organizations
alternatives.concept: Study how organizations develop products, market them, manage people and make financial decisions. Apply research methods to customer and organizational questions, and study how policy and ethics shape business.
alternatives.labelReason: Study how organizations develop products, market them, manage people and make financial decisions. Apply research methods to customer and organizational questions, and study how policy and ethics shape business.
progression: Business and economics foundations precede financial markets and strategic applications. Research Methods & Statistics precedes experimental methods and market research.

alternatives.label: Finance, Economics and Business Analytics
alternatives.concept: Study financial statements, markets, banking and economic decisions. Use programming, statistics, econometrics and machine learning to analyze evidence for business decisions.
alternatives.labelReason: Study financial statements, markets, banking and economic decisions. Use programming, statistics, econometrics and machine learning to analyze evidence for business decisions.
alternatives.distinctness: Study financial statements, markets, banking and economic decisions. Use programming, statistics, econometrics and machine learning to analyze evidence for business decisions. Each plan has 10 courses absent from the other when compared with option 1.
progression: Economics and mathematical foundations precede financial markets, econometrics and behavioral economics. Programming and introductory data science precede machine learning.

alternatives.label: Sustainable Business and Organizational Change
alternatives.concept: Study how businesses develop products and adapt to environmental change. Combine entrepreneurship and leadership with life-cycle assessment, circular design, sustainability governance and public policy.
alternatives.labelReason: Study how businesses develop products and adapt to environmental change. Combine entrepreneurship and leadership with life-cycle assessment, circular design, sustainability governance and public policy.
alternatives.distinctness: Study how businesses develop products and adapt to environmental change. Combine entrepreneurship and leadership with life-cycle assessment, circular design, sustainability governance and public policy. Each plan has 9 courses absent from the other when compared with option 1. Each plan has 15 courses absent from the other when compared with option 2.
progression: Sustainability foundations precede resource recovery and renewable design. Business foundations precede advanced entrepreneurship and governance. Product design and strategic management support later entrepreneurship and policy work.

candidates.label: Accounting, finance & economics for business decisions
Business resilience & leadership of societal transitions

selection.assessment: The broad option retains a business, strategy, people and marketing spine. The finance option strengthens economics and quantitative analysis. The transition option adds policy, circular production and stakeholder perspectives. Pairwise differences are 1/2: 10 courses, 1/3: 9 courses, 2/3: 15 courses. Marketing, consumer design and market research support customer study within the closest option. Available supply-chain content is embedded in general business, trade and circular production; a separate coherent supply-chain and marketing direction would largely repeat the closest option and lack specialist operations depth.

blocks: Both develop entrepreneurial thinking, business models and venture planning.
Both study organizational strategy. UCR emphasizes digital transformation.
UCR develops products from customer needs through prototyping. Open Universiteit covers innovation management more broadly.
Open Universiteit requires a dedicated management and organization course. UCR introduces related topics in its business gateway.
Open Universiteit studies open innovation across organizations in a dedicated course.
Both examine motivation, group behavior and organizational culture.
Both develop leadership skills. UCR emphasizes personal leadership and self-awareness.
Open Universiteit provides a dedicated course in organization theory.
Open Universiteit offers a dedicated human resource management course. UCR covers related topics in organizational psychology.
Open Universiteit teaches organizational consulting and coaching in a dedicated course.
Open Universiteit studies workplace resilience. UCR examines related questions of psychological safety and leadership under pressure.
Both examine marketing strategy and customer behavior.
Open Universiteit has a dedicated business-to-business marketing course.
Both develop the use of financial statements for business analysis.
Both develop financial decision-making. UCR focuses on financial markets, institutions and risk.
Both introduce economic reasoning about firms, markets and the wider economy.
Open Universiteit offers a dedicated management accounting course.
Open Universiteit offers dedicated sustainable finance.
Both teach research design and quantitative methods. Open Universiteit uses a longer, group-based practicum.
Both develop applied empirical research. UCR focuses on market research and customers.
Open Universiteit requires a 15 EC thesis. UCR independent research is optional and outside the scheduled degree.
Both address governance. UCR focuses on international business and corporate responsibility.
Open Universiteit teaches business ethics. UCR develops general ethical reasoning.
Open Universiteit provides a dedicated supply chain management course.
Open Universiteit provides a separate course on supply chain resilience.
Both develop academic study, writing and communication skills.

notes.text: The plans share study of strategy, accounting and finance, marketing, leadership and research. Open Universiteit offers dedicated supply chain management, human resource management, sustainable finance and consulting courses. It also requires a 15 EC thesis. UCR offers optional independent research alongside its course-based plans.

audience.programmeDescription: Open Universiteit’s Dutch-taught, part-time Business Administration bachelor covers organizations, strategy, finance, marketing and research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The 2026–2027 curriculum preserves the 30 EC free elective space. The UCR plans emphasize broad business study, finance and analytics, or sustainable business and organizational change.
